items.change: The party arrived at Brandonsford following a treasure map whose marked locations they did not recognize, in land unknown to them.
items.impact_basis: The single beat establishes the party's arrival and their map-driven goal, framing the campaign's premise without any discovery about the treasure.
items.lasting_basis: The beat sets up an unfound treasure the party is actively pursuing, which should drive later Sessions.

items.change: Reginald warned that a trickster Clurichen comes from the riverbanks into town every night and should be avoided.
items.impact_basis: Reginald's warning introduces a new local danger but nothing happened with it yet.
items.lasting_basis: The nightly Clurichen likely ties into the vanishing ale and Sir Phidipaldi's claims, so it is likely to come up again.

items.change: The party learned a black dragon is terrorizing Brandonsford and Eric the Reeve offered 1000 gold for its body, though Sir Phidipaldi insulted and challenged Eric.
items.impact_basis: Eric's 1000-gold bounty, Lady Hilda's offer to join, George's lost arm and Gill's sons hunting the dragon together give the party a major new goal and foe.
items.lasting_basis: The standing bounty, the hireable Hilda and the strained relationship with Eric after the glove slap will shape later Sessions.

items.change: The party learned that shipments to Brandonsford have stopped for weeks or months, leaving the town short of goods.
items.impact_basis: Bentley's overdue shipment, Warwick's empty shop and Quinn's report reveal a town-wide supply problem whose cause is unknown.
items.lasting_basis: The unexplained missing shipments are an open mystery likely tied to the dragon and likely to come up again.

items.change: Drop Dead Ned offered himself and his killer wasp for hire at 100 gold a week, and Dr. Uriah said he would think about it.
items.impact_basis: Ned's murderous hire offer introduces a potential, dangerous ally, but no agreement was made.
items.lasting_basis: Dr. Uriah left the offer open, so Ned may return as hireling or threat.

items.change: Farmer Gill offered Dunk the mule Shamus for 100 gold, and Dunk is considering trading work for it while staying in Gill's barn.
items.impact_basis: An offer of an ordinary mount was made and not accepted, a small adjustment.
items.lasting_basis: The pending mule offer and Dunk's lodging with Gill may come up again but are minor.

items.change: Sir Phidipaldi agreed to Quinn's 100-gold deal to stage a fake ale shipment to catch Bentley, whom Quinn blames for his vanishing stock.
items.impact_basis: Sir Phidipaldi struck a paid agreement with Quinn and planned the water-bottle ruse, clearly changing the situation.
items.lasting_basis: The agreed deal remains to be carried out and pits the party against Bentley, so it will likely shape the next Session.

items.change: Bentley banned Sir Phidipaldi from his tavern for the night, sending him to the Golden Egg while his friends stayed.
items.impact_basis: Bentley's intervention split the party's lodging for one night after the argument with Eric.
items.lasting_basis: The ejection lasts only the night, though it may color Bentley's view of Sir Phidipaldi.
